A clean reinstall almost always\n * succeeds. This helper centralises that retry so every call site picks\n * it up.\n */\n\n/**\n * @param {(specifier: string) => Promise<unknown>} use - the use-m loader.\n * @param {string} specifier - the npm specifier to load (e.g. `'getenv'`).\n * @param {object} [options]\n * @param {number} [options.attempts=3] - total attempts including the first try.\n * @param {(path: string) => Promise<void>} [options.cleanup] - injectable cleanup\n *   for the corrupted install directory (defaults to recursive `rm`).\n * @param {(ms: number) => Promise<void>} [options.sleep] - injectable backoff used\n *   between attempts when the global `npm install -g` itself failed.\n * @param {number} [options.backoffMs=1000] - base backoff, doubled per attempt.\n * @param {(message: string) => void} [options.log] - diagnostics sink; defaults to\n *   `console.error` when `HIVE_MIND_USE_M_DEBUG` is set, otherwise silent.\n * @returns {Promise<unknown>} the module returned by use-m.\n */\nexport const useWithRetry = async (use, specifier, options = {}) => {\n  const attempts = options.attempts ?? 3;\n  const cleanup = options.cleanup ?? defaultCleanup;\n  const sleep = options.sleep ?? defaultSleep;\n  const backoffMs = options.backoffMs ?? 1000;\n  const log = options.log ?? defaultLog;\n  const importModule = options.importModule ?? defaultImport;\n  const extraArgs = options.args ?? There is nothing to delete; just\n      // back off and let npm try again.\n      if (isTransientInstallError(error)) {\n        await sleep(backoffMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1));\n        continue;\n      }\n      const corruptedPath = extractCorruptedFilePath(error);\n      if (corruptedPath) {\n        try {\n          // Two failure modes:\n          //   * \"Failed to import module from '<file>'\" — corruptedPath is a file\n          //     inside the use-m alias dir (e.g. /.../getenv-v-latest/index.js).\n          //   * \"Failed to resolve the path to 'pkg' from '<dir>'\" — corruptedPath\n          //     is the alias dir itself (e.g. /.../links-notation-v-latest).\n          // For files, walk up to the alias dir; otherwise remove the dir as-is.\n          await cleanup(resolveAliasDir(corruptedPath));\n          // Remember the file so the next attempt can bypass Node's poisoned\n          // module cache if use-m hands us the same path again.\n          cleanedImportPath = /Failed to import module from '/.test(error?.message ?? It is another incomplete-tree\nstate: enough of the alias exists for use-m to reuse it, but not enough for Node\nto evaluate it.\n\n## Root causes\n\n1. **Incomplete alias install.** A versioned global package directory was visible\n   before or after an interrupted/partial installation, while an internal file\n   was absent. The evidence does not identify whether interruption, concurrent\n   mutation, or filesystem behavior caused the partial tree; all produce the\n   same recoverable state.\n2. **Classifier gap.** `isCorruptInstallError()` recognized syntax corruption,\n   invalid `package.json`, and use-m resolution failure, but not Node's\n   `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` nested as the cause of use-m's import wrapper.\n3. **Sticky reuse.** use-m sees the alias directory as installed, so without\n   removing it a later load can reuse the same incomplete tree.\n\n## Selected solution\n\nRecognize `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` only when it is the cause of use-m's\n`Failed to import module from '…'` error. This guard avoids retrying arbitrary\napplication-level missing imports. Existing shared recovery then:\n\n1. extracts the entry-point path from the wrapper;\n2. walks upward to the `<package>-v-<version>` alias;\n3. removes that entire alias;\n4. calls use-m again, causing a clean install;\n5. uses the existing cache-busted import fallback if Node replays a failed ESM\n   evaluation for the same entry URL.\n\nBecause `ensureUseM()` wraps `globalThis.use`, this applies to all dependency\nimports rather than only `command-stream` or the failing `/fix` path.\n\n## Alternatives\n\n- **Retry only in `/fix`:** rejected because the failure happens during shared\n  module loading and affects every command.\n- **Add retries at every `use(...)`:** rejected because it duplicates policy and\n  misses future call sites.\n- **Rely only on CI/Docker pre-installation:** insufficient for runtime installs\n  and for aliases that become incomplete after the pre-install step.\n- **Move every dynamic dependency into local `package.json`:** potentially more\n  reproducible, but a broad architectural migration that does not repair the\n  current global alias cache. It can be evaluated separately.\n- **Retry all `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`:** rejected because permanently broken\n  package releases and application coding errors should remain visible. The\n  use-m wrapper guard keeps the workaround narrow.\n\n## Verification strategy\n\nThe unit test recreates the exact nested error and asserts both classification\nand whole-alias cleanup. The hermetic experiment asks Node to import an entry\nwhose relative dependency is absent, confirms `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, then\nsimulates a clean reinstall during shared recovery. [2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] *** Add File: docs/case-studies/issue-2113/upstream-use-m-cleanup-report.md
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +# Recursive alias cleanup can fail with ENOTEMPTY because rm has no retry budget
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +## Problem
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +`use-m@8.14.3` added corrupt-alias self-healing in #67. A production run made
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +after that release reached the new repair path, but repair itself failed:
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +```text
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +Failed to remove corrupt npm alias '.../command-stream-v-latest'.
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +Caused by: Error: ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +'.../command-stream-v-latest/examples' (code: ENOTEMPTY)
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +```
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +Environment: Node 20.20.2, Linux, Docker-in-Docker. Full downstream log:
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +https://gist.github.com/konard/154eaf009bdf41cd722fe902cfbcb10c
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +The shared `removePackageAlias()` calls:
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +```js
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +await rm(packagePath, { recursive: true, force: true });
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +```
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +Node's `fsPromises.rm` documentation says `ENOTEMPTY` is retryable when
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +`recursive` is true, but `maxRetries` defaults to zero. A concurrent installer
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +or another filesystem mutation can therefore win between directory enumeration
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +and removal, and the transient race escapes from the recovery path.
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +## Reproduction
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +The downstream stress reproduction keeps writing into an alias while it is
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +removed:
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2113-39f0b66307a2/experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +On Node 20/Linux:
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +```text
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +default rm reproduced ENOTEMPTY on attempt 1
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +retry-budget rm completed without leaving the alias behind
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +```
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +The exact production error shape is also covered by an automated downstream
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +regression test.
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +## Suggested fix
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +Give recursive alias removal an explicit retry budget:
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +```js
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +await rm(packagePath, {
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +  recursive: true,
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +  force: true,
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +  maxRetries: 5,
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +  retryDelay: 100,
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +});
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +```
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +Because `removePackageAlias()` is shared, this covers both cleanup after a
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +failed install and cleanup before corrupt-alias repair. A regression test can
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +inject or provoke `ENOTEMPTY` and verify that removal is retried before the
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +repair fails.
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +## Downstream workaround
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +Hive Mind classifies only use-m's exact `Failed to remove
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +(corrupt|incomplete) npm alias ...` wrapper when its cause is one of Node's
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +documented recursive-rm retry codes. It extracts the alias, removes it with an
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +explicit retry budget, and calls `use()` again:
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2114
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] +Related: #66 and #67.
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.680Z] [INFO] *** End Patch

[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +Because `removePackageAlias()` is shared, this covers both cleanup after a
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +failed install and cleanup before corrupt-alias repair. A regression test can
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +inject or provoke `ENOTEMPTY` and verify that removal is retried before the
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +repair fails.
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +

[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +

[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +(corrupt|incomplete) npm alias ...` wrapper when its cause is one of Node's
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +documented recursive-rm retry codes. It extracts the alias, removes it with an
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +explicit retry budget, and calls `use()` again:
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2114
[2026-07-28T20:44:53.700Z] [INFO] +

[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -## Root causes
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +An `npm pack command-stream@0.17.2 --dry-run --json` audit found all three files
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +in the published tarball: `src/$.mjs` (12,555 bytes), `src/$.trace.mjs` (1,439
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +bytes), and `src/terminal-capture.mjs` (13,500 bytes). The tag and tarball agree.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +There is therefore no evidence of a `command-stream` packaging defect.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +### Cleanup failure after the upstream fix
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +`use-m@8.14.3`, published at 19:28 UTC, added the requested corrupt-alias
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +self-heal. The 20:04 UTC run reached it but failed while removing the alias:
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +```text
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +Failed to remove corrupt npm alias '.../command-stream-v-latest'.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +Caused by: ENOTEMPTY .../command-stream-v-latest/examples
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +```
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +The upstream helper called `rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +Node documents that `ENOTEMPTY`, `EBUSY`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, and `EPERM` are
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +retried only when recursive removal has a positive `maxRetries`; the default is
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +zero. The concurrent writer stress experiment reproduces `ENOTEMPTY` with the
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +zero-retry call and succeeds with five retries. The evidence proves a mutation
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +race or equivalent transient filesystem condition, but does not identify which
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +process performed the competing mutation.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +## Root causes and gaps
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  1. **Incomplete alias install.** A versioned global package directory was visible
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]     before or after an interrupted/partial installation, while an internal file
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -   was absent. The evidence does not identify whether interruption, concurrent
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -   mutation, or filesystem behavior caused the partial tree; all produce the
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -   same recoverable state.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +   was absent. Two different missing files from a complete tarball rule out a
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +   deterministic missing-file release.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  2. **Classifier gap.** `isCorruptInstallError()` recognized syntax corruption,
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]     invalid `package.json`, and use-m resolution failure, but not Node's
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]     `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` nested as the cause of use-m's import wrapper.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  3. **Sticky reuse.** use-m sees the alias directory as installed, so without
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]     removing it a later load can reuse the same incomplete tree.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +4. **Zero-retry cleanup.** The new use-m repair and Hive Mind's downstream
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +   cleanup both relied on `fsPromises.rm()` defaults, so `ENOTEMPTY` escaped
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +   rather than receiving the retry behavior Node provides.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +5. **New wrapper signature.** Hive Mind did not classify or extract the alias
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +   from use-m 8.14.3's `Failed to remove corrupt npm alias ...` error.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  ## Selected solution
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -Recognize `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` only when it is the cause of use-m's
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -`Failed to import module from '…'` error. This guard avoids retrying arbitrary
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -application-level missing imports. Existing shared recovery then:
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +The shared recovery recognizes two narrow signatures:
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -1. extracts the entry-point path from the wrapper;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -2. walks upward to the `<package>-v-<version>` alias;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -3. removes that entire alias;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -4. calls use-m again, causing a clean install;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -5. uses the existing cache-busted import fallback if Node replays a failed ESM
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -   evaluation for the same entry URL.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +1. `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` only when it is the cause of use-m's exact
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +   `Failed to import module from '…'` wrapper;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +2. use-m's exact `Failed to remove (corrupt|incomplete) npm alias '…'.` wrapper
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +   only when its cause is one of Node's documented recursive-rm retry codes.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +It then extracts or derives the `<package>-v-<version>` alias, removes it with
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +`recursive`, `force`, five retries, and 100 ms linear retry delay, and calls
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +use-m again. The existing cache-busted import fallback remains available if
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +Node replays a failed ESM evaluation for the same entry URL.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  Because `ensureUseM()` wraps `globalThis.use`, this applies to all dependency
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  imports rather than only `command-stream` or the failing `/fix` path.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  ## Alternatives
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +- **Pin `command-stream`:** rejected because the 0.17.2 registry tarball contains
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +  every missing file. An older version can be left incomplete by the same
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +  install/mutation failure.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +- **Pin use-m 8.14.2:** rejected because it removes upstream self-healing and its
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +  downstream cleanup still had the same zero-retry `rm` behavior.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +- **Use only use-m 8.14.3 self-healing:** insufficient because the supplied
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +  post-release log demonstrates its cleanup can fail before reinstall.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  - **Retry only in `/fix`:** rejected because the failure happens during shared
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]    module loading and affects every command.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  - **Add retries at every `use(...)`:** rejected because it duplicates policy and
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] @@
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  - **Retry all `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`:** rejected because permanently broken
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]    package releases and application coding errors should remain visible. The
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]    use-m wrapper guard keeps the workaround narrow.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  ## Verification strategy
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -The unit test recreates the exact nested error and asserts both classification
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -and whole-alias cleanup. The hermetic experiment asks Node to import an entry
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -whose relative dependency is absent, confirms `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, then
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -simulates a clean reinstall during shared recovery. Full default tests, lint,
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] -format, syntax, and file-size checks provide regression coverage.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +The unit tests recreate both exact wrapper errors and assert classification,
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +path extraction, whole-alias cleanup, and retry. A separate unit test verifies
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +the default cleanup passes `maxRetries: 5` and `retryDelay: 100` to recursive
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +`rm`. The hermetic missing-file experiment confirms Node's real
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` shape. The concurrent writer experiment provokes real
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +`ENOTEMPTY` and verifies retry-budget cleanup. Full default tests, lint, format,
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +syntax, and file-size checks provide regression coverage.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +The original incomplete-install problem was reported and fixed in
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +[use-m #66](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66) /
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +[PR #67](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/pull/67). The cleanup race is
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.917Z] [INFO] +reported separately as [use-m #68](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68).

[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +### Incomplete aliases
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +The alias entry point existed in two independent runs:
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  ```text
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  .../command-stream-v-latest/src/$.mjs

[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -but Node could not resolve a relative file imported from it:
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +but Node could not resolve two different relative files imported from it:
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  ```text
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  .../command-stream-v-latest/src/terminal-capture.mjs

[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  ```
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  This distinguishes the failure from issue #2092's truncated `$.mjs`
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  (`SyntaxError`) and failed `npm install -g`. It is another incomplete-tree
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  state: enough of the alias exists for use-m to reuse it, but not enough for Node
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  to evaluate it.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -## Root causes
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +An `npm pack command-stream@0.17.2 --dry-run --json` audit found all three files
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +in the published tarball: `src/$.mjs` (12,555 bytes), `src/$.trace.mjs` (1,439
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +bytes), and `src/terminal-capture.mjs` (13,500 bytes). The tag and tarball agree.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +There is therefore no evidence of a `command-stream` packaging defect.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +### Cleanup failure after the upstream fix
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +`use-m@8.14.3`, published at 19:28 UTC, added the requested corrupt-alias
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +self-heal. The 20:04 UTC run reached it but failed while removing the alias:
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +```text
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +Failed to remove corrupt npm alias '.../command-stream-v-latest'.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +Caused by: ENOTEMPTY .../command-stream-v-latest/examples
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +```
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +The upstream helper called `rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +Node documents that `ENOTEMPTY`, `EBUSY`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, and `EPERM` are
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +retried only when recursive removal has a positive `maxRetries`; the default is
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +zero. The concurrent writer stress experiment reproduces `ENOTEMPTY` with the
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +zero-retry call and succeeds with five retries. The evidence proves a mutation
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +race or equivalent transient filesystem condition, but does not identify which
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +process performed the competing mutation.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +## Root causes and gaps
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  1. **Incomplete alias install.** A versioned global package directory was visible
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]     before or after an interrupted/partial installation, while an internal file
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -   was absent. The evidence does not identify whether interruption, concurrent
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -   mutation, or filesystem behavior caused the partial tree; all produce the
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -   same recoverable state.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +   was absent. Two different missing files from a complete tarball rule out a
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +   deterministic missing-file release.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  2. **Classifier gap.** `isCorruptInstallError()` recognized syntax corruption,
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]     invalid `package.json`, and use-m resolution failure, but not Node's
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]     `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` nested as the cause of use-m's import wrapper.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  3. **Sticky reuse.** use-m sees the alias directory as installed, so without
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]     removing it a later load can reuse the same incomplete tree.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +4. **Zero-retry cleanup.** The new use-m repair and Hive Mind's downstream
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +   cleanup both relied on `fsPromises.rm()` defaults, so `ENOTEMPTY` escaped
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +   rather than receiving the retry behavior Node provides.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +5. **New wrapper signature.** Hive Mind did not classify or extract the alias
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +   from use-m 8.14.3's `Failed to remove corrupt npm alias ...` error.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  ## Selected solution
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -Recognize `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` only when it is the cause of use-m's
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -`Failed to import module from '…'` error. This guard avoids retrying arbitrary
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -application-level missing imports. Existing shared recovery then:
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +The shared recovery recognizes two narrow signatures:
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -1. extracts the entry-point path from the wrapper;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -2. walks upward to the `<package>-v-<version>` alias;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -3. removes that entire alias;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -4. calls use-m again, causing a clean install;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -5. uses the existing cache-busted import fallback if Node replays a failed ESM
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -   evaluation for the same entry URL.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +1. `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` only when it is the cause of use-m's exact
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +   `Failed to import module from '…'` wrapper;
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +2. use-m's exact `Failed to remove (corrupt|incomplete) npm alias '…'.` wrapper
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +   only when its cause is one of Node's documented recursive-rm retry codes.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +It then extracts or derives the `<package>-v-<version>` alias, removes it with
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +`recursive`, `force`, five retries, and 100 ms linear retry delay, and calls
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +use-m again. The existing cache-busted import fallback remains available if
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +Node replays a failed ESM evaluation for the same entry URL.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  Because `ensureUseM()` wraps `globalThis.use`, this applies to all dependency
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  imports rather than only `command-stream` or the failing `/fix` path.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  ## Alternatives
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +- **Pin `command-stream`:** rejected because the 0.17.2 registry tarball contains
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +  every missing file. An older version can be left incomplete by the same
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +  install/mutation failure.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +- **Pin use-m 8.14.2:** rejected because it removes upstream self-healing and its
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +  downstream cleanup still had the same zero-retry `rm` behavior.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +- **Use only use-m 8.14.3 self-healing:** insufficient because the supplied
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +  post-release log demonstrates its cleanup can fail before reinstall.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  - **Retry only in `/fix`:** rejected because the failure happens during shared
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]    module loading and affects every command.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  - **Add retries at every `use(...)`:** rejected because it duplicates policy and
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] @@
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  - **Retry all `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`:** rejected because permanently broken
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]    package releases and application coding errors should remain visible. The
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]    use-m wrapper guard keeps the workaround narrow.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  ## Verification strategy
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO]  
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -The unit test recreates the exact nested error and asserts both classification
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -and whole-alias cleanup. The hermetic experiment asks Node to import an entry
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -whose relative dependency is absent, confirms `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, then
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -simulates a clean reinstall during shared recovery. Full default tests, lint,
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] -format, syntax, and file-size checks provide regression coverage.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +The unit tests recreate both exact wrapper errors and assert classification,
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +path extraction, whole-alias cleanup, and retry. A separate unit test verifies
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +the default cleanup passes `maxRetries: 5` and `retryDelay: 100` to recursive
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +`rm`. The hermetic missing-file experiment confirms Node's real
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` shape. The concurrent writer experiment provokes real
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +`ENOTEMPTY` and verifies retry-budget cleanup. Full default tests, lint, format,
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +syntax, and file-size checks provide regression coverage.
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +The original incomplete-install problem was reported and fixed in
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +[use-m #66](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66) /
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +[PR #67](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/pull/67). The cleanup race is
[2026-07-28T20:46:52.970Z] [INFO] +reported separately as [use-m #68](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68).

[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] # Recursive alias cleanup can fail with ENOTEMPTY because rm has no retry budget

[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] ## Problem
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] `use-m@8.14.3` added corrupt-alias self-healing in #67. A production run made
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] after that release reached the new repair path, but repair itself failed:
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] ```text
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] Failed to remove corrupt npm alias '.../command-stream-v-latest'.

[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] '.../command-stream-v-latest/examples' (code: ENOTEMPTY)
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] ```
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] Environment: Node 20.20.2, Linux, Docker-in-Docker. Full downstream log:
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] https://gist.github.com/konard/154eaf009bdf41cd722fe902cfbcb10c
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] The shared `removePackageAlias()` calls:
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] ```js
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] await rm(packagePath, { recursive: true, force: true });
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] ```
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] Node's `fsPromises.rm` documentation says `ENOTEMPTY` is retryable when
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] `recursive` is true, but `maxRetries` defaults to zero. A concurrent installer
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] or another filesystem mutation can therefore win between directory enumeration
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] and removal, and the transient race escapes from the recovery path.
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] ## Reproduction
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO]

[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] On Node 20/Linux:
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO]

[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] ```
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] 
[2026-07-28T20:54:28.023Z] [INFO] The exact production error shape is also covered by an automated downstream

The shared loader recognizes wrapped\ninternal `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and retryable use-m alias-cleanup failures,\nremoves the whole versioned alias with a bounded retry budget, and retries the\ndependency load for every existing and future `use(...)` call site.\n\n## Contents\n\n- [`timeline.md`](timeline.md) reconstructs the observed sequence and prior fixes.\n- [`requirements.md`](requirements.md) maps every issue requirement to evidence.\n- [`analysis.md`](analysis.md) documents root cause, scope, alternatives, and plan.\n- [`research.md`](research.md) records upstream and platform research.\n- [`raw/`](raw/) preserves all three supplied logs and the package/release audit.\n- [`upstream-use-m-cleanup-report.md`](upstream-use-m-cleanup-report.md) preserves\n  the report filed as [use-m #68](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68).\n- [`../../../../experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-missing-transitive.mjs`](../../../../experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-missing-transitive.mjs)\n  is a hermetic missing-file reproduction.\n- [`../../../../experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs`](../../../../experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs)\n  reproduces `ENOTEMPTY` and verifies retry-budget cleanup.\n\n## Verification\n\n```bash\nnode experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-missing-transitive.mjs\nnode experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs\nnode tests/test-use-with-retry.mjs\n```\nFILE docs/case-studies/issue-2113/analysis.md\n# Root-cause analysis\n\n## Observed failures\n\n### Incomplete aliases\n\nThe alias entry point existed in two independent runs:\n\n```text\n.../command-stream-v-latest/src/$.mjs\n```\n\nbut Node could not resolve two different relative files imported from it:\n\n```text\n.../command-stream-v-latest/src/terminal-capture.mjs\n.../command-stream-v-latest/src/$.trace.mjs\ncode: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND\n```\n\nThis distinguishes the failure from issue #2092's truncated `$.mjs`\n(`SyntaxError`) and failed `npm install -g`. It is another incomplete-tree\nstate: enough of the alias exists for use-m to reuse it, but not enough for Node\nto evaluate it.\n\nAn `npm pack command-stream@0.17.2 --dry-run --json` audit found all three files\nin the published tarball: `src/$.mjs` (12,555 bytes), `src/$.trace.mjs` (1,439\nbytes), and `src/terminal-capture.mjs` (13,500 bytes). The tag and tarball agree.\nThere is therefore no evidence of a `command-stream` packaging defect.\n\n### Cleanup failure after the upstream fix\n\n`use-m@8.14.3`, published at 19:28 UTC, added the requested corrupt-alias\nself-heal. The 20:04 UTC run reached it but failed while removing the alias:\n\n```text\nFailed to remove corrupt npm alias '.../command-stream-v-latest'.\nCaused by: ENOTEMPTY .../command-stream-v-latest/examples\n```\n\nThe upstream helper called `rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true })`.\nNode documents that `ENOTEMPTY`, `EBUSY`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, and `EPERM` are\nretried only when recursive removal has a positive `maxRetries`; the default is\nzero. The concurrent writer stress experiment reproduces `ENOTEMPTY` with the\nzero-retry call and succeeds with five retries. The evidence proves a mutation\nrace or equivalent transient filesystem condition, but does not identify which\nprocess performed the competing mutation.\n\n## Root causes and gaps\n\n1. **Incomplete alias install.** A versioned global package directory was visible\n   before or after an interrupted/partial installation, while an internal file\n   was absent. Two different missing files from a complete tarball rule out a\n   deterministic missing-file release.\n2. **Classifier gap.** `isCorruptInstallError()` recognized syntax corruption,\n   invalid `package.json`, and use-m resolution failure, but not Node's\n   `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` nested as the cause of use-m's import wrapper.\n3. **Sticky reuse.** use-m sees the alias directory as installed, so without\n   removing it a later load can reuse the same incomplete tree.\n4. **Zero-retry cleanup.** The new use-m repair and Hive Mind's downstream\n   cleanup both relied on `fsPromises.rm()` defaults, so `ENOTEMPTY` escaped\n   rather than receiving the retry behavior Node provides.\n5. **New wrapper signature.** Hive Mind did not classify or extract the alias\n   from use-m 8.14.3's `Failed to remove corrupt npm alias ...` error.\n\n## Selected solution\n\nThe shared recovery recognizes two narrow signatures:\n\n1. `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` only when it is the cause of use-m's exact\n   `Failed to import module from '…'` wrapper;\n2. use-m's exact `Failed to remove (corrupt|incomplete) npm alias '…'.` wrapper\n   only when its cause is one of Node's documented recursive-rm retry codes.\n\nIt then extracts or derives the `<package>-v-<version>` alias, removes it with\n`recursive`, `force`, five retries, and 100 ms linear retry delay, and calls\nuse-m again. The existing cache-busted import fallback remains available if\nNode replays a failed ESM evaluation for the same entry URL.\n\nBecause `ensureUseM()` wraps `globalThis.use`, this applies to all dependency\nimports rather than only `command-stream` or the failing `/fix` path.\n\n## Alternatives\n\n- **Pin `command-stream`:** rejected because the 0.17.2 registry tarball contains\n  every missing file. An older version can be left incomplete by the same\n  install/mutation failure.\n- **Pin use-m 8.14.2:** rejected because it removes upstream self-healing and its\n  downstream cleanup still had the same zero-retry `rm` behavior.\n- **Use only use-m 8.14.3 self-healing:** insufficient because the supplied\n  post-release log demonstrates its cleanup can fail before reinstall.\n- **Retry only in `/fix`:** rejected because the failure happens during shared\n  module loading and affects every command.\n- **Add retries at every `use(...)`:** rejected because it duplicates policy and\n  misses future call sites.\n- **Rely only on CI/Docker pre-installation:** insufficient for runtime installs\n  and for aliases that become incomplete after the pre-install step.\n- **Move every dynamic dependency into local `package.json`:** potentially more\n  reproducible, but a broad architectural migration that does not repair the\n  current global alias cache. It can be evaluated separately.\n- **Retry all `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`:** rejected because permanently broken\n  package releases and application coding errors should remain visible. The\n  use-m wrapper guard keeps the workaround narrow.\n\n## Verification strategy\n\nThe unit tests recreate both exact wrapper errors and assert classification,\npath extraction, whole-alias cleanup, and retry. A separate unit test verifies\nthe default cleanup passes `maxRetries: 5` and `retryDelay: 100` to recursive\n`rm`. The hermetic missing-file experiment confirms Node's real\n`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` shape. The concurrent writer experiment provokes real\n`ENOTEMPTY` and verifies retry-budget cleanup. Full default tests, lint, format,\nsyntax, and file-size checks provide regression coverage.\n\nThe original incomplete-install problem was reported and fixed in\n[use-m #66](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66) /\n[PR #67](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/pull/67). The cleanup race is\nreported separately as [use-m #68](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68).\nFILE docs/case-studies/issue-2113/requirements.md\n# Requirements\n\n| ID  | Requirement                                                           | Resolution                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |\n| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| R1  | Make dependency imports stable or retry them.                         | Classify wrapped internal `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and retryable use-m cleanup errors; shared recovery removes the alias with a bounded filesystem retry budget and reloads it.                                                              |\n| R2  | Apply the fix in every relevant place.                                | `ensureUseM()` wraps the single global loader; no per-call-site changes are needed. Issue #2113 added a fourth concrete\n  corrupt-tree signature: a wrapped `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for an internal file.\n  The exact evidence, reproduction, guard, and suggested fix were added in\n  [this upstream report](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66#issuecomment-5107282485).\n- [use-m PR #67](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/pull/67) merged at\n  19:26 UTC and `use-m@8.14.3` was published at 19:28 UTC. The follow-up is reported as\n  [use-m #68](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68).\n- use-m installs npm aliases such as\n  `command-stream-v-latest@npm:command-stream@latest`, then dynamically imports\n  the resolved entry point. Hive Mind's narrow shared wrapper remains a\n  downstream defense for older versions and cleanup failures.\n\n## command-stream\n\n- The current release is `command-stream@0.17.2`, published on 2026-07-26 and\n  matching repository tag `js-v0.17.2`.\n- `npm pack command-stream@0.17.2 --dry-run --json` reports 466 entries and the\n  registry integrity recorded in `raw/dependency-audit.json`. Pinning an older command-stream cannot prevent an interrupted or\n  concurrently-mutated alias, so no command-stream defect was reported.\n\n## Node.js\n\n- [Node's ESM documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html) says file URLs are\n  resolved as modules and a nonexistent resolved file produces Module Not\n  Found. This matches the missing relative `terminal-capture.mjs` evidence.\n- The same documentation states ESM has a separate cache from `require.cache`\n  and that query-string variants load as distinct modules. That supports the\n  existing cache-busting recovery retained from issue #2092.\n- [Node's `fsPromises.rm` documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fspromisesrmpath-options)\n  explicitly lists `ENOTEMPTY`, `EBUSY`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, and `EPERM` as\n  retryable during recursive removal. `maxRetries` defaults to zero and\n  `retryDelay` defaults to 100 ms. The selected five-retry budget uses this\n  platform-supported mechanism.\n- Node's promise-based filesystem documentation also warns that concurrent\n  modifications are not synchronized. The cleanup stress experiment models\n  that condition directly.\n\n## npm\n\n- [npm install documentation](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/install/) confirms an\n  install includes a package and its dependencies, and global mode writes under\n  the configured prefix.\n- [npm package-spec documentation](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/using-npm/package-spec/)\n  defines `<alias>@npm:<name>` as the alias syntax reified in `node_modules`,\n  matching use-m's versioned alias layout.\n- [npm pack documentation](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-pack)\n  defines `--dry-run` as a no-change report of what pack/publish would include.\n  This makes the registry tarball inventory appropriate evidence when checking\n  whether command-stream omitted either missing module.\n\n## Related Hive Mind work\n\n- PR #2093 is the closest implementation: it centralized recovery at the loader,\n  removed whole aliases, retried transient installs, and handled ESM caching.\n- PR #1725 pre-installs use-m packages with retry to avoid concurrent CI install\n  races. It reduces exposure but cannot replace runtime self-healing.\n- Issues #1710 and #1712 supplied the original corruption classifier.\nFILE docs/case-studies/issue-2113/timeline.md\n# Timeline\n\n| Time (UTC)          | Event                                                                                                                                                                                             |\n| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| 2026-04-28          | Issues #1710/#1712 establish recovery for truncated JavaScript, unresolved entry points, and invalid package configuration.                                                                       |\n| 2026-04-29          | PR #1725 adds retrying pre-installation for CI races, but runtime loading remains use-m's responsibility.                                                                                         |\n| 2026-07-20          | Issue #2092 shows recovery only covered a few call sites. A production run made\nafter that release reached the new repair path, but repair itself failed:\n\n```text\nFailed to remove corrupt npm alias '.../command-stream-v-latest'.\nCaused by: Error: ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir\n'.../command-stream-v-latest/examples' (code: ENOTEMPTY)\n```\n\nEnvironment: Node 20.20.2, Linux, Docker-in-Docker. Full downstream log:\nhttps://gist.github.com/konard/154eaf009bdf41cd722fe902cfbcb10c\n\nThe shared `removePackageAlias()` calls:\n\n```js\nawait rm(packagePath, { recursive: true, force: true });\n```\n\nNode's `fsPromises.rm` documentation says `ENOTEMPTY` is retryable when\n`recursive` is true, but `maxRetries` defaults to zero. A concurrent installer\nor another filesystem mutation can therefore win between directory enumeration\nand removal, and the transient race escapes from the recovery path.\n\n## Reproduction\n\nThe downstream stress reproduction keeps writing into an alias while it is\nremoved:\n\nhttps://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2113-39f0b66307a2/experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs\n\nOn Node 20/Linux:\n\n```text\ndefault rm reproduced ENOTEMPTY on attempt 1\nretry-budget rm completed without leaving the alias behind\n```\n\nThe exact production error shape is also covered by an automated downstream\nregression test.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nGive recursive alias removal an explicit retry budget:\n\n```js\nawait rm(packagePath, {\n  recursive: true,\n  force: true,\n  maxRetries: 5,\n  retryDelay: 100,\n});\n```\n\nBecause `removePackageAlias()` is shared, this covers both cleanup after a\nfailed install and cleanup before corrupt-alias repair. A regression test can\ninject or provoke `ENOTEMPTY` and verify that removal is retried before the\nrepair fails.\n\n## Downstream workaround\n\nHive Mind classifies only use-m's exact `Failed to remove\n(corrupt|incomplete) npm alias ...` wrapper when its cause is one of Node's\ndocumented recursive-rm retry codes. It extracts the alias, removes it with an\nexplicit retry budget, and calls `use()` again:\n\nhttps://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2114\n\nRelated: [use-m #66](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66) and\n[use-m PR #67](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/pull/67).\nFILE docs/case-studies/issue-2113/raw/dependency-audit.json\n{\n  \"auditedAt\": \"2026-07-28T20:39:37Z\",\n  \"commandStream\": {\n    \"version\": \"0.17.2\",\n    \"publishedAt\": \"2026-07-26T23:45:46.988Z\",\n    \"repositoryTag\": \"js-v0.17.2\",\n    \"repositoryCommit\": \"1132c71\",\n    \"npmIntegrity\": \"sha512-SEHSZgtfV6/llMw7mm0q/1w559EZd56rPmcGjkTWEkFwjtunqMM20qh8cr33S7CQ6FRfIVoiMjTPyvvnFOTvcw==\",\n    \"npmEntryCount\": 466,\n    \"requiredFiles\": [\n      {\n        \"path\": \"src/$.mjs\",\n        \"size\": 12555\n      },\n      {\n        \"path\": \"src/$.trace.mjs\",\n        \"size\": 1439\n      },\n      {\n        \"path\": \"src/terminal-capture.mjs\",\n        \"size\": 13500\n      }\n    ]\n  },\n  \"useM\": {\n    \"previousVersion\": \"8.14.2\",\n    \"fixedVersion\": \"8.14.3\",\n    \"publishedAt\": \"2026-07-28T19:28:19.389Z\",\n    \"repositoryTag\": \"v8.14.3\",\n    \"repositoryCommit\": \"8c5a55d144d8655efa805d02a3f234e8dfd6a9d4\",\n    \"upstreamIssue\": \"https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66\",\n    \"upstreamPullRequest\": \"https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/pull/67\",\n    \"cleanupFollowUpIssue\": \"https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68\"\n  }\n}\nFILE experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs\n#!/usr/bin/env node\n\n/**\n * Issue #2113 follow-up: provoke the ENOTEMPTY race observed when use-m@8.14.3\n * removes an alias while another process is still mutating that directory.\n *\n * This is an opt-in stress experiment, not a default-suite test. await rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 25 });\n  return { error, resurrected };\n};\n\nlet observedDefaultFailure = null;\nfor (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 20; Both files are\n+present in the published `command-stream@0.17.2` tarball, establishing that the\n+global alias was incomplete rather than the package release.\n+\n+The recovery introduced for issues #1710, #1712, and #2092 was already applied\n+at the shared `ensureUseM()` bootstrap, so every relevant dependency load used\n+it. The remaining gap was classification: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` nested under\n+use-m's `Failed to import module from ...` wrapper was not recognized as an\n+incomplete install. It therefore failed immediately without cleanup or retry.\n+\n+`use-m@8.14.3` then shipped upstream self-healing, but the next supplied run\n+exposed a second gap: recursive alias removal failed with `ENOTEMPTY`.\n+`fsPromises.rm()` retries that code only when `maxRetries` is explicitly\n+positive; use-m and Hive Mind both used the zero-retry default.\n+\n+This change covers both exact signatures. The shared loader recognizes wrapped\n+internal `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and retryable use-m alias-cleanup failures,\n+removes the whole versioned alias with a bounded retry budget, and retries the\n+dependency load for every existing and future `use(...)` call site.\n+\n+## Contents\n+\n+- [`timeline.md`](timeline.md) reconstructs the observed sequence and prior fixes.\n+- [`requirements.md`](requirements.md) maps every issue requirement to evidence.\n+- [`analysis.md`](analysis.md) documents root cause, scope, alternatives, and plan.\n+- [`research.md`](research.md) records upstream and platform research.\n+- [`raw/`](raw/) preserves all three supplied logs and the package/release audit.\n+- [`upstream-use-m-cleanup-report.md`](upstream-use-m-cleanup-report.md) preserves\n+  the report filed as [use-m #68](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68).\n+- [`../../../../experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-missing-transitive.mjs`](../../../../experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-missing-transitive.mjs)\n+  is a hermetic missing-file reproduction.\n+- [`../../../../experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs`](../../../../experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs)\n+  reproduces `ENOTEMPTY` and verifies retry-budget cleanup.\n+\n+## b/docs/case-studies/issue-2113/analysis.md\n@@ -0,0 +1,118 @@\n+# Root-cause analysis\n+\n+## Observed failures\n+\n+### Incomplete aliases\n+\n+The alias entry point existed in two independent runs:\n+\n+```text\n+.../command-stream-v-latest/src/$.mjs\n+```\n+\n+but Node could not resolve two different relative files imported from it:\n+\n+```text\n+.../command-stream-v-latest/src/terminal-capture.mjs\n+.../command-stream-v-latest/src/$.trace.mjs\n+code: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND\n+```\n+\n+This distinguishes the failure from issue #2092's truncated `$.mjs`\n+(`SyntaxError`) and failed `npm install -g`. It is another incomplete-tree\n+state: enough of the alias exists for use-m to reuse it, but not enough for Node\n+to evaluate it.\n+\n+An `npm pack command-stream@0.17.2 --dry-run --json` audit found all three files\n+in the published tarball: `src/$.mjs` (12,555 bytes), `src/$.trace.mjs` (1,439\n+bytes), and `src/terminal-capture.mjs` (13,500 bytes). The tag and tarball agree.\n+There is therefore no evidence of a `command-stream` packaging defect.\n+\n+### Cleanup failure after the upstream fix\n+\n+`use-m@8.14.3`, published at 19:28 UTC, added the requested corrupt-alias\n+self-heal. The 20:04 UTC run reached it but failed while removing the alias:\n+\n+```text\n+Failed to remove corrupt npm alias '.../command-stream-v-latest'.\n+Caused by: ENOTEMPTY .../command-stream-v-latest/examples\n+```\n+\n+The upstream helper called `rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true })`.\n+Node documents that `ENOTEMPTY`, `EBUSY`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, and `EPERM` are\n+retried only when recursive removal has a positive `maxRetries`; the default is\n+zero. The concurrent writer stress experiment reproduces `ENOTEMPTY` with the\n+zero-retry call and succeeds with five retries. The evidence proves a mutation\n+race or equivalent transient filesystem condition, but does not identify which\n+process performed the competing mutation.\n+\n+## Root causes and gaps\n+\n+1. **Incomplete alias install.** A versioned global package directory was visible\n+   before or after an interrupted/partial installation, while an internal file\n+   was absent. Two different missing files from a complete tarball rule out a\n+   deterministic missing-file release.\n+2. **Classifier gap.** `isCorruptInstallError()` recognized syntax corruption,\n+   invalid `package.json`, and use-m resolution failure, but not Node's\n+   `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` nested as the cause of use-m's import wrapper.\n+3. **Sticky reuse.** use-m sees the alias directory as installed, so without\n+   removing it a later load can reuse the same incomplete tree.\n+4. **Zero-retry cleanup.** The new use-m repair and Hive Mind's downstream\n+   cleanup both relied on `fsPromises.rm()` defaults, so `ENOTEMPTY` escaped\n+   rather than receiving the retry behavior Node provides.\n+5. **New wrapper signature.** Hive Mind did not classify or extract the alias\n+   from use-m 8.14.3's `Failed to remove corrupt npm alias ...` error.\n+\n+## Selected solution\n+\n+The shared recovery recognizes two narrow signatures:\n+\n+1. `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` only when it is the cause of use-m's exact\n+   `Failed to import module from '…'` wrapper;\n+2. use-m's exact `Failed to remove (corrupt|incomplete) npm alias '…'.` wrapper\n+   only when its cause is one of Node's documented recursive-rm retry codes.\n+\n+It then extracts or derives the `<package>-v-<version>` alias, removes it with\n+`recursive`, `force`, five retries, and 100 ms linear retry delay, and calls\n+use-m again. The existing cache-busted import fallback remains available if\n+Node replays a failed ESM evaluation for the same entry URL.\n+\n+Because `ensureUseM()` wraps `globalThis.use`, this applies to all dependency\n+imports rather than only `command-stream` or the failing `/fix` path.\n+\n+## Alternatives\n+\n+- **Pin `command-stream`:** rejected because the 0.17.2 registry tarball contains\n+  every missing file. An older version can be left incomplete by the same\n+  install/mutation failure.\n+- **Pin use-m 8.14.2:** rejected because it removes upstream self-healing and its\n+  downstream cleanup still had the same zero-retry `rm` behavior.\n+- **Use only use-m 8.14.3 self-healing:** insufficient because the supplied\n+  post-release log demonstrates its cleanup can fail before reinstall.\n+- **Retry only in `/fix`:** rejected because the failure happens during shared\n+  module loading and affects every command.\n+- **Add retries at every `use(...)`:** rejected because it duplicates policy and\n+  misses future call sites.\n+- **Rely only on CI/Docker pre-installation:** insufficient for runtime installs\n+  and for aliases that become incomplete after the pre-install step.\n+- **Move every dynamic dependency into local `package.json`:** potentially more\n+  reproducible, but a broad architectural migration that does not repair the\n+  current global alias cache. It can be evaluated separately.\n+- **Retry all `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`:** rejected because permanently broken\n+  package releases and application coding errors should remain visible. The\n+  use-m wrapper guard keeps the workaround narrow.\n+\n+## Verification strategy\n+\n+The unit tests recreate both exact wrapper errors and assert classification,\n+path extraction, whole-alias cleanup, and retry. A separate unit test verifies\n+the default cleanup passes `maxRetries: 5` and `retryDelay: 100` to recursive\n+`rm`. The hermetic missing-file experiment confirms Node's real\n+`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` shape. The concurrent writer experiment provokes real\n+`ENOTEMPTY` and verifies retry-budget cleanup. Full default tests, lint, format,\n+syntax, and file-size checks provide regression coverage.\n+\n+The original incomplete-install problem was reported and fixed in\n+[use-m #66](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66) /\n+[PR #67](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/pull/67). The cleanup race is\n+reported separately as [use-m #68](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68).\ndiff --git a/docs/case-studies/issue-2113/raw/dependency-audit.json A production run made\n+after that release reached the new repair path, but repair itself failed:\n+\n+```text\n+Failed to remove corrupt npm alias '.../command-stream-v-latest'.\n+Caused by: Error: ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir\n+'.../command-stream-v-latest/examples' (code: ENOTEMPTY)\n+```\n+\n+Environment: Linux, Docker-in-Docker. The launcher reports Node 24.3.0; the\n+affected global alias is under the NVM 20.20.2 prefix. Full downstream log:\n+https://gist.github.com/konard/154eaf009bdf41cd722fe902cfbcb10c\n+\n+The shared `removePackageAlias()` calls:\n+\n+```js\n+await rm(packagePath, { recursive: true, force: true });\n+```\n+\n+Node's `fsPromises.rm` documentation says `ENOTEMPTY` is retryable when\n+`recursive` is true, but `maxRetries` defaults to zero. A concurrent installer\n+or another filesystem mutation can therefore win between directory enumeration\n+and removal, and the transient race escapes from the recovery path.\n+\n+## Reproduction\n+\n+The downstream stress reproduction keeps writing into an alias while it is\n+removed:\n+\n+https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2113-39f0b66307a2/experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs\n+\n+On Node 20/Linux (the downstream development environment):\n+\n+```text\n+default rm reproduced ENOTEMPTY on attempt 1\n+retry-budget rm completed without leaving the alias behind\n+```\n+\n+The exact production error shape is also covered by an automated downstream\n+regression test.\n+\n+## Suggested fix\n+\n+Give recursive alias removal an explicit retry budget:\n+\n+```js\n+await rm(packagePath, {\n+  recursive: true,\n+  force: true,\n+  maxRetries: 5,\n+  retryDelay: 100,\n+});\n+```\n+\n+Because `removePackageAlias()` is shared, this covers both cleanup after a\n+failed install and cleanup before corrupt-alias repair. A regression test can\n+inject or provoke `ENOTEMPTY` and verify that removal is retried before the\n+repair fails.\n+\n+## Downstream workaround\n+\n+Hive Mind classifies only use-m's exact `Failed to remove\n+(corrupt|incomplete) npm alias ...` wrapper when its cause is one of Node's\n+documented recursive-rm retry codes. It extracts the alias, removes it with an\n+explicit retry budget, and calls `use()` again:\n+\n+https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2114\n+\n+Related: [use-m #66](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66) and\n+[use-m PR #67](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/pull/67).\ndiff --git a/experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs b/experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs\nnew file mode 100644\nindex 000000000..ce1deba44\n--- /dev/null\n+++ b/experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs\n@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@\n+#!/usr/bin/env node\n+\n+/**\n+ * Issue #2113 follow-up: provoke the ENOTEMPTY race observed when use-m@8.14.3\n+ * removes an alias while another process is still mutating that directory.\n+ *\n+ * This is an opt-in stress experiment, not a default-suite test. [2026-07-28T21:54:13.460Z] [STDOUT] [{"createdAt":"2026-07-28T16:21:51Z","headRefName":"issue-2113-39f0b66307a2","isDraft":false,"number":2114,"state":"OPEN","title":"fix(2113): recover incomplete use-m aliases and cleanup races","updatedAt":"2026-07-28T21:53:44Z","url":"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2114"}]
[2026-07-28T21:54:13.476Z] [INFO]   ✅ Found pull request #2114: "fix(2113): recover incomplete use-m aliases and cleanup races"
[2026-07-28T21:54:13.928Z] [STDOUT] ## Problem

`fix --ci-cd` failed while loading `command-stream` from a global use-m alias in three supplied production runs:

1. the alias contained `src/$.mjs` but lacked its relative import `src/terminal-capture.mjs`;
2. another run lacked `src/$.trace.mjs` instead;
3. after `use-m@8.14.3` added corrupt-alias self-healing, repair failed while removing the alias with `ENOTEMPTY`.

Hive Mind's shared retry classifier did not recognize the wrapped internal `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Both use-m's new repair and Hive Mind's downstream cleanup also called recursive `fsPromises.rm()` with Node's default `maxRetries: 0`, allowing the transient cleanup race to escape.

## Solution

- recognize `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` only when it is the cause of use-m's exact `Failed to import module from ...` wrapper;
- recognize use-m's exact corrupt/incomplete-alias cleanup wrapper only for Node's documented recursive-removal retry codes;
- extract or derive the whole versioned alias, remove it with `recursive`, `force`, five retries, and a 100 ms retry delay, then call use-m again;
- retain shared `ensureUseM()` wrapping, so every current and future `use(...)` call site receives the recovery;
- emit cleanup failures through the existing opt-in `HIVE_MIND_USE_M_DEBUG` trace instead of silently discarding them;
- add a patch changeset, regression tests, and two reusable real-filesystem experiments.

## Dependency ownership and pinning

An `npm pack command-stream@0.17.2 --dry-run --json` audit found all 466 published entries, including `src/$.mjs`, `src/$.trace.mjs`, and `src/terminal-capture.mjs`; tag `js-v0.17.2` agrees with the tarball. The varying absent file therefore identifies incomplete aliases, not a command-stream packaging defect. Pinning command-stream cannot prevent the same partial-install state.

Pinning use-m to 8.14.2 would remove upstream self-healing while leaving the downstream zero-retry cleanup gap. The original install problem was reported in [use-m #66](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/66) and fixed by [use-m PR #67](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/pull/67). The post-release cleanup race is separately reported with the production evidence, reproduction, and suggested fix in [use-m #68](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/68).

## Reproduction and verification

Regression-first evidence:

- the cleanup follow-up started with 35 passing and 3 failing cases before implementation;
- `node tests/test-use-with-retry.mjs` — 39/39 passed after the fix;
- `node experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-missing-transitive.mjs` — produces the real wrapped `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, removes the alias, and recovers on attempt 2;
- `node experiments/issue-2113/reproduce-cleanup-race.mjs` — zero-retry removal reproduces `ENOTEMPTY`; retry-budget removal completes without leaving the alias behind.

Final local gates:

- `npm test` — all 354 selected test files passed;
- `npm run lint`;
- `npm run format:check`;
- `bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh`;
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`;
- `git diff --check`.

## Preserved evidence

The [issue #2113 case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-2113-39f0b66307a2/docs/case-studies/issue-2113) contains all three complete supplied logs, package/release audit data, timeline, requirement map, root-cause analysis, alternatives, online/upstream research, and the preserved use-m #68 report body.
